fields.meta_title: Reference Check Form Template and Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: What to ask on a reference check form, how to rate each answer, and an app that emails references the questions and stores every reply.
fields.hero_description: A reference check form is the script for asking a candidate's former managers about their work. Emergent builds the form, sends it or opens it for a call, and saves each reply.
fields.features_subheading: The versions that rank are Word files and PDFs. Emergent keeps their sections and saves each answer as data.
fields.feature_1:
Who is asking, and about whom

Opens with the candidate and the role, then names the reference and the company where the two worked together. Each reference becomes its own entry under the candidate's record.
fields.feature_2:
How the reference knows the candidate

Asks how long the two worked together and in what capacity before any rating. A peer from one project and a manager of four years carry different weight in the final decision.
fields.feature_3:
Dates and title, beside the resume

Records the dates and final title the reference confirms next to what the candidate wrote on the resume. A missing year or a different job title shows up well before an offer.
fields.feature_4:
A 1-5 rating for each work area

Rates each area the role needs, such as reliability or judgment, on one shared scale with a note under it. Two people who call someone dependable can still be two points apart.
fields.feature_5:
The rehire question, asked plainly

Ends by asking whether the reference would hire or work with the candidate again, and why. A hesitant yes is worth writing down word for word, as it often says more than a rating.
fields.feature_6:
Export the app to GitHub

Pushes the full app and its database schema to your GitHub on paid plans. Engineers can host it on your own servers or connect it to the applicant tracking system recruiters use.

fields.usecase_heading: Reference Checks Across Four Hiring Teams
fields.tab_content_1:
The same eight questions on every call

General manager candidates at Harborview Restaurant Group each name three references, and the hiring manager phones all of them. The form is the call script: eight questions in a fixed order, with a notes box under each. Two calls are logged for Priya Nair, and the last one is booked for 10:30 AM.
fields.tab_content_2:
A link for each reference, a nudge after two days

Caregivers often list families they worked for alongside former supervisors. Brightwell Home Care emails every reference a short questionnaire to answer on a phone: five work areas rated 1-5, plus the rehire question. Anyone who has not replied after two days gets a reminder. Two of three are in for Marcus Bell.
fields.tab_content_3:
A no on rehire puts a callback on the principal's list

Principals at Lakemont School District hire most teachers in a short spring window. Every reference answers the rehire question, and the app reads each answer. When a reference answers no, the principal gets a task to call that person back and ask why before any offer leaves the district office.
fields.tab_content_4:
The board reads all three references side by side

A volunteer search committee at Riverbend Food Bank is hiring a finance director. For each finalist, the app builds a summary page with three references' ratings in adjacent columns and the average for every work area. Committee members read it before the board votes on an offer.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Reference Check Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps for the person who makes the hiring call. Write the questions once, then ask them the same way of every reference.
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Rate each area on one scale
fields.howto_step_1_des: Let finalists know you will contact their references, and ask before calling a current employer. UC Berkeley's HR guidance tells hiring managers to give candidates advance notice. Check references after the interview, once you know what you still need to learn.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask each finalist for contact details for every reference and a line on how they worked together. Request at least one former direct manager. A manager can speak to reliability in ways a peer or a client usually cannot.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Draft a short set of questions tied to the job and ask every reference the same ones in the same order. Start with how long and in what capacity the person knew the candidate, the way the University of Northern Iowa sample opens.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the four or five areas that matter for the role and rate each on a 1-5 scale. Write down what a 1 and a 5 mean for each. A note under every rating carries the reason, which matters most when two references disagree.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Leave out what you cannot ask
fields.howto_step_5_des: Skip questions about age, religion, disability or pregnancy, even when a reference raises them. Laws the EEOC enforces bar hiring decisions based on those traits. Questions about family plans invite the same problem. Keep every question on the work itself.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Some companies confirm only dates of employment and job title, as a matter of policy. Rules on what a former employer may share differ by state. Record the limit as the answer, then move on to the next name the candidate gave you.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Store each completed reference check with the candidate's record, including for people you did not hire. Federal rules require employers to keep hiring records for one year. Ask counsel whether your state or your contracts set a longer period.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is blank reference forms from HR offices (UNI, Berkeley, Fairbanks North Star Borough, Community College of Philadelphia, a community foundation), SHRM's phone form, AIHR and Indeed templates, and one Jotform template. All carry the same parts: candidate and reference details, how the reference knows the candidate, dates and title, performance questions and a rehire question. This page lays out those sections with a 1-5 rating on each area, then builds what a Word file cannot: a call script that saves notes per question, an emailed questionnaire with reminders, a callback task when a reference says no to rehire, and a one-page summary of all references for the decision maker.
tab_stories: A restaurant group hiring a general manager uses the form as the call script; the hiring manager types notes under each of eight questions, and the candidate's record shows two of three calls logged with the third booked for 10:30 AM.

A nonprofit search committee hiring a finance director gets one page per finalist with all three references' ratings side by side and the average for each area, ready before the board votes.
